title: CASE Expression
description: Learn how to use CASE expressions for conditional logic in SQL queries.

data.text: The CASE expression evaluates a list of conditions and returns one of the multiple specified results. It has two formats: simple CASE and searched CASE.

data.title: Simple CASE expression
data.content: Maps order status codes to readable labels.
data.code:
CASE order_status
    WHEN 1 THEN 'Pending'
    WHEN 2 THEN 'Processing'
    WHEN 3 THEN 'Rejected'
    WHEN 4 THEN 'Completed'
END AS order_status

data.title: Searched CASE expression
data.code:
CASE
    WHEN SUM(quantity * list_price) <= 500 THEN 'Very Low'
    WHEN SUM(quantity * list_price) <= 1000 THEN 'Low'
    WHEN SUM(quantity * list_price) <= 5000 THEN 'Medium'
    WHEN SUM(quantity * list_price) <= 10000 THEN 'High'
    ELSE 'Very High'
END AS order_priority

data.title: CASE Expression Key Points
points: CASE is an expression usable in SELECT, WHERE, GROUP BY, and HAVING.
Simple CASE compares for equality; searched CASE evaluates Boolean expressions.
The ELSE clause is optional and returns NULL if omitted.
CASE expressions can be nested inside aggregate functions.
